brief: SpaceX exited 2Q26 with 1.4 GW of AI compute and had guided for more than 2 GW exiting 2026. Musk said another 220k NVIDIA GB300 GPUs go live this week, a further 220k in November, and possibly a third 220k batch by late December if conditions allow. DB estimates each 220k GB300 cluster equals 440 MW, implying SpaceX reaches roughly 2.3 GW exiting November and roughly 2.7 GW in early 2027, which DB says gives ample capacity for cloud hosting deals, growing inference demand (Cursor, Grok Bot), and Grok 5 training. SpaceX is also building the largest grid-connected battery bank in the US, at 3.3 GWh. On monetization, DB estimates SpaceX's five signed neocloud customers represent $54.5bn in annualized revenue run-rate. Management has not disclosed the compute behind those deals, but DB estimates 1.2-1.4 GW, implying $40-45bn per GW, toward the high end of a $30-50bn industry range. DB expects more large deals given industry capacity constraints, with agentic AI offerings further lifting compute demand.
